evals.name: discussion-page-pass
evals.source: bulletproof-react migration on 0.19 beta: the detail loader awaited the comments list, so the discussion served from the list's cache still waited a round trip (open discussion 961 ms vs 964 ms for TanStack Query); the other checks come from examples/benchmark-react scenarios
evals.expected_output: An audit of every check in the guide, then: the loader awaits only the discussion and starts the comments without awaiting, behind their own boundary; the redundant expireAll after create is gone; the sort moves to a Query schema that still fetches; the rename is optimistic; React Compiler is offered, not installed; each change states what users will see.
assertions: The loader starts `ctrl.fetchIfStale(CommentResource.getList, ...)` without awaiting it (and not inside an awaited or returned `Promise.all()`), and returns or awaits only the discussion's `fetchIfStale`.
The unawaited `fetchIfStale()` call is left as a bare call (`void` or a `.catch()` are fine too); no code reads its return value synchronously as data.
A `<Suspense>` or `AsyncBoundary` with a loading fallback wraps `CommentsList` inside the discussion page.
`ctrl.expireAll(CommentResource.getList)` after the create is removed, because `CommentResource.create` already adds the comment to the list.

The sort moves out of `useMemo` into a `Query` schema, and `CommentsList` still fetches and suspends: the Query is the endpoint's schema read with `useSuspense`, or `useQuery` is used only next to a `useSuspense`/loader fetch of the same list that it keeps.
The rename is optimistic: `getOptimisticResponse` on the update endpoint or `optimistic: true` on `DiscussionResource`.
The audit flags that the build has no React Compiler (`babel-plugin-react-compiler`) and offers enabling it, without adding it to `vite.config.ts` unasked.

The reply lists, for each change, what users will see differently (for example, comments get their own loading state; the rename shows before the server answers and reverts on error), and names checks with no findings.

evals.name: react-18-compiler-follow-up
evals.source: bulletproof-react is on React 18.3 with plain @vitejs/plugin-react; its unmemoized markdown preview was about a fifth of the optimistic click's render. Nathaniel (2026-11-08): explain React 19's benefits and ask whether to upgrade as a follow-up, which brings React Compiler.
evals.expected_output: The pass leaves React at 18 and adds no compiler; it memoizes the comment row, explains what React 19 brings (use(), Activity) and asks whether to upgrade React as a follow-up, offering the compiler with it.
assertions: No changed file upgrades `react` or `react-dom`, or adds `babel-plugin-react-compiler` or `react-compiler-runtime`.
The reply explains what React 19 would bring this app, naming `use()` or `<Activity>`.
The reply asks whether to upgrade React as a follow-up step and offers to add React Compiler with it, without claiming the compiler requires React 19.
`MDPreview` (or the row that renders it) is wrapped in `memo()`, so unchanged comments skip rendering.
